prompt: Write an email to convey the following information. The person is call Jack and works at Nvidia. I saw them demo a product called NeMo-Guardrails. This product is using negative examples to prevent an llm from answering queries that are out of scope, unsafe or problematic in any way. I want the email to ask them if they have considered a positive approach instead? I think the approach of listing all the don't is going to be long and arduous. An approach that would use the llm to first determine if the query is within the scope of acceptable and then proceed sounds better to me.  I am wondering if they have considered this approach and if so why it was not working. My name is Marc.
response:
Subject: Inquiry About NeMo-Guardrails and Alternative Approaches

Hi Jack,

I hope this email finds you well. My name is Marc, and I recently had the opportunity to see Nvidia's demo of NeMo-Guardrails. I was quite impressed with the product and its innovative use of negative examples to prevent an LLM from responding to out-of-scope, unsafe, or problematic queries.

However, I was wondering if the team has considered an alternative approach that focuses on positive reinforcement rather than negative examples. Specifically, I believe that listing all the "don'ts" could become quite extensive and cumbersome over time. An approach where the LLM first determines if a query falls within the scope of acceptable responses and then proceeds to answer could potentially be more efficient and scalable.

I am curious to know if this positive approach has been considered and, if so, what challenges or limitations were encountered that led to the decision to use negative examples instead.

Thank you for your time, and I look forward to your insights.

Best regards,  
Marc
